content: The document titled Lymphatic Filariasis Managing Morbidity and Preventing Disability: An Aide-Mémoire for National Programme Managers (Second Edition) was published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2021. It is available in both electronic and print versions, with respective ISBNs 978-92-4-001706-1 and 978-92-4-001707-8. The manual provides detailed guidance on managing morbidity and preventing disability (MMDP) related to lymphatic filariasis (LF). It includes strategies for national monitoring and evaluation plans, as well as annexes with tools such as the Dreyer Seven-Stage Classification System for lymphedema, simplified staging for community health workers, and management protocols for acute attacks and advanced lymphedema (elephantiasis). The publication also introduces new tools and resources to assist countries in planning and expanding MMDP services and documenting criteria for validating LF elimination as a public health problem. The glossary defines key terms used in the manual, such as abscess, acute attack, acute dermatolymphangioadenitis (ADLA), adenolymphangitis (ADL), and others. It explains clinical manifestations of LF, including lymphedema, hydrocele, and chyluria, and provides definitions for terms like hygiene, mass drug administration, and preventive chemotherapy. The manual also outlines the roles of community-based care and family home-based care in improving the quality of life for affected individuals. The Global Programme to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis (GPELF), launched by WHO in 2000, is highlighted as a key initiative. By the end of 2018, LF was endemic in 72 countries and territories, with an estimated 892 million people at risk of infection. The manual underscores the importance of MMDP as a critical component of the global effort to eliminate LF, particularly as countries approach validation of LF elimination as a public health problem. It provides a comprehensive toolkit of clinical, operational, and managerial standard operating procedures to support the planning and implementation of MMDP activities. The second edition of the manual incorporates updates and new content based on feedback from reviewers and contributors. It includes additional figures, tables, and tools to enhance clarity and usability. The manual is the result of collaboration between the WHO Department of Control of Neglected Tropical Diseases and the WHO Department of Emergency and Essential Surgical Care, with funding support from the USAID MMDP Project. It aims to provide national programme managers, healthcare workers, researchers, and other stakeholders with a concise and practical resource for addressing the chronic manifestations of LF and improving care for affected individuals.
